title: Expanded Form Splitter
description: Split a decimal into its place value, decimal and fractional forms at once, and drag an expanded form back into standard form with zeros in the missing places.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

writeup.why: Write a decimal in place value, decimal and fractional expanded forms, and write an expanded form back in standard form, putting zeros in missing places.
writeup.look: Digit tiles over a place strip at the top, three labelled rows of parts under them, and a tray of parts on the last phase.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Expanded Form Splitter' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x sixty-four, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: how many parts the decimal splits into, one for each digit that is not 0. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x sixty-four, y 202. The digit tiles run across the top of the working area at y 230, each 90 across, deep blue, with the large near-black point between Ones and Tenths and the place strip under them at y 330. The three rows run below at y 410, y 500 and y 590, each labelled at x 110 with its form: Place value form, Decimal form, Fractional form. Each part slides down from the digit it came from and lands in its row joined by plus signs; the Place value form row opens with the word is. A zero digit's part drops a little way and fades to half strength beside the words adds nothing. The Join button sits at the right end of each row, and the total it gives lands green under the row. On the last phase the tray runs along y 660, and a place left empty between parts lights grey and takes a 0 labelled Place holder. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is twelve number keys three across with a point key, a plus key and a fraction bar key, for setting a decimal or typing a part or a standard form into the answer slot. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. A decimal or fraction the question gives is deep blue, with the shaded parts that show it. The result the working reaches, a decimal, a fraction, a sum, a difference or what is left, is green, with its shaded parts. Ten of one place traded for one of the next, a carry in adding or a trade in taking away, is vermilion. A zero written after the point to line decimals up is violet, and so is the point written after a whole number before those zeros. The part taken away, used or poured out is rose. The digit, place or step being worked on now, and the first place where two decimals differ, are amber. A zero holding a place open inside a number is grey, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded part stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the decimal point is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each of those readings survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label, Given, Answer, Carry, Trade, Added zero, Taken away, Left or Place holder, before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The card shows the last decimal with its three expanded forms under it, each joined back up to the same number.

writeup.delight: On the second phase, when the child taps Join, the parts of the row slide back up into their tiles one after another with a soft click each, and the decimal lights green as the last one lands.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with the tiles in place. On the first three phases a decimal sits on the tiles over the place strip, and the row for that phase's form is empty below it. On the fourth the place strip is empty and the parts of an expanded form wait in the tray. One thing moves, once: the Split button, or the first part in the tray, gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any decimal split into all three forms and joined back up, and any expanded form built back from the tray. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on place value form, decimal form, fractional form and standard form.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The hidden place names light up one by one from the point, and the asked part's name is written into the row.
Phase 2: The places after the point light up one by one up to the asked digit, and its worth is written on the Decimal card.
Phase 3: Each place after the point shows its denominator, the zero holding its place, and the asked part is written on the Fraction card.
Phase 4: Every part slides to the place it names, each empty place takes a grey 0, and the number is written on the Decimal card.

voice.opening: One decimal, ready to be split three ways.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: tap a digit to change it, then tap Split or Build.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: Three forms, one number, and it went back together.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }
